query: CHP olağanüstü kurultay çağrı heyeti Sulh Hukuk Mahkemesi başvuru karar - latest status as of late June / early July 2026. Has Özgür Özel's team filed the application under Civil Code Art 75 requesting appointment of a 3-person çağrı heyeti to convene a CHP extraordinary congress? Has any court issued a decision?
answer:
I've completed the research. Here's a summary of my findings:

## Summary

**The application has been filed, but no court decision has been issued.**

**Key findings:**

1. **Filing confirmed**: On **14 July 2026** (Tuesday), Özgür Özel's elected CHP leadership team filed the application with the **Ankara Sulh Hukuk Mahkemesi** requesting a **3-person çağrı heyeti** to convene the extraordinary congress.

2. **Legal basis**: The petition explicitly invokes **Turkish Civil Code (Medeni Kanun) Article 75/2** — which allows a civil court judge, on a member's application, to appoint three members to convene a general assembly when management fails to do so.

3. **What was requested**: (a) three delegates designated as the çağrı heyeti; (b) authority to set congress place/day/time/agenda and carry out call procedures; and (c) a **tedbir kararı (interim measure)** ordering the committee to begin its duties.

4. **No court decision** had been publicly announced as of 13-14 July 2026.

5. **Backing**: 833 kurultay delegates (>2/3 of the delegate body) submitted notarized signatures on 17 June 2026; the Genel Merkez (under Kılıçdaroğlu, following the "mutlak butlan" decision) did not act on them, triggering the court application.

**Important caveat on timeframe**: The question referenced "late June / early July 2026," but the actual formal filing occurred **14 July 2026**. As of early July, the application was being prepared/announced (via Spokesperson Zeynel Emre) but not yet formally submitted. A separate, earlier proceeding — an istinaf court rejection of a different application concerning Kılıçdaroğlu's blocking tedbir kararı — occurred on 26 June 2026.

key_facts: Özgür Özel's CHP leadership team filed the çağrı heyeti application with the Ankara Sulh Hukuk Mahkemesi on 14 July 2026.
The application was filed under Turkish Civil Code (Medeni Kanun) Article 75 (Art. 75/2), requesting appointment of a 3-person çağrı heyeti (calling committee) to convene an extraordinary congress.
833 CHP kurultay delegates signed notarized petitions demanding the olağanüstü kurultay, representing more than two-thirds of the total delegate body.
The signatures were delivered to CHP Genel Başkanlığı on 17 June 2026, within the party bylaws' required 15-day window.
The petition also requested a tedbir kararı (interim measure) ordering the 3-member committee to begin its duties and set the congress place, day, time, and agenda.
As of 13-14 July 2026, NO court decision (acceptance, rejection, or interim measure) had been publicly announced on this application.

The dispute follows the 'mutlak butlan' (absolute nullity) decision after which Kemal Kılıçdaroğlu returned to CHP Genel Başkanlığı; the Genel Merkez did not process the delegate signatures, triggering the court application.
CHP Spokesperson Zeynel Emre announced the plan to apply to the Sulh Hukuk Mahkemesi (~13 July 2026) and framed the delegates' will as legally binding on management.
In a separate earlier proceeding, on 26 June 2026 an istinaf (appellate) court rejected an application related to Kılıçdaroğlu's tedbir kararı blocking the extraordinary congress.
The query's stated timeframe (late June/early July 2026) predates the actual formal filing date of 14 July 2026.
